subject: CONSTANT RECORD clause
notes: kb/Work/PB881.md - SR2 is a rule over an OPERAND ROLE ('shall be specified as a receiving data item'), so it is written once, in ExpressionBinder.ResolveReceiving (DataBinder.RejectConstantStore, COBOL1548), and every verb binder now states each operand's role by calling ResolveReceiving or ResolveSending - never ctx.Refs.Resolve, which screens nothing (ReceivingResolutionDriftTests fails a binder under Verbs/ that does). The sweep moved every receiving operand that had bypassed the chokepoint: INSPECT identifier-1 under REPLACING/CONVERTING (14.9.22.3 SR8 keeps Format 1's TALLYING-only identifier-1 SENDING), READ INTO (sequential and keyed) and RETURN INTO, the CORRESPONDING receiving group, SEARCH VARYING identifier-2 (14.9.37.4 GR1), INVOKE RETURNING (three arms) and BY REFERENCE arguments (typed and universal), the SET object-reference / data-pointer / program-pointer / function-pointer receivers, SET ... TO LOCALE's save target, ALLOCATE RETURNING, FREE and SET UP/DOWN pointer receivers. ACCEPT (the note's second site) had already been routed by PB429 (3fffacb61). The negatives pin four of the formerly bypassing arms at 2002/2014/2023; the positive pins the SENDING roles that stay legal (INSPECT TALLYING of a constant -> CN=0004 unchanged, MOVE CORRESPONDING from a constant group). The CONSTANT RECORD clause is COBOL-2002, so the rule has no population at 85. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Constants.cs#RejectConstantStore (kb/Work PB1418 turned the reporting RejectConstantStore into the non-reporting ConstantStoreProhibition, asked by ExpressionBinder.ReceivingPlaceBar (the place half of the receiving-prohibition table ResolveReceiving reports and PermitsReceiving asks))
